findings.description: budget_cents_max: false is replaced with 600 by yq's // operator before validation. Consequently, a malformed maximum leaves budget_scale: diff enabled instead of applying the documented fixed fallback.
findings.failure_mode: With configured budget 150, estimate 200, scale diff and maximum false, the gate permits dispatch with effective budget 240. The required fixed fallback would refuse the run because 200 exceeds 150.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the raw maximum and default only for null or absence. Validate other values before enabling diff scaling.

findings.description: Python scope detection treats the closing line of a multiline function signature as the end of the function when that line shares the def's indentation. For example, an ordinary signature ending with an unindented '):' terminates the recorded scope before its body.
findings.failure_mode: Defect sites and citations within that function body receive no enclosing scope. A valid citation more than three lines from the defect is marked missed despite satisfying the advertised same-function rule, changing the grade and pass result.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Python syntax parsing to obtain function spans, or track signature continuation through the start of the body before applying indentation-based termination.

findings.description: A yq failure (config file absent or unreadable, yq missing) is substituted with the literal 'unreadable', which is neither '!!null' nor empty, so the function falls through to CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true, logs a WARN that budget_scale='(a unreadable, not a string)' is not fixed or diff, and later stamps budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max into every envelope. The surrounding reads in load_adversarial_config all carry '|| echo <default>' fallbacks, so the no-config path is one the script already tolerates.
findings.failure_mode: On a host without .loa.config.yaml (or without yq) every dissent run emits a spurious malformed-config warning and the envelope metadata changes shape, contradicting the documented 'absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged' guarantee and tripping any consumer that diffs envelopes against the shipped form.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a yq failure as absent: capture the exit status separately (e.g. `_bt=$(yq ... 2>/dev/null) || return 0`) or add 'unreadable' to the early-return case, so only a key that is actually present sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET.

findings.description: Under budget_scale: diff the effective budget is min(max(conf, scaled), budget_cents_max). When budget_cents_max (default 600) is below the configured budget_cents or the CLI --budget value, the result is smaller than the operator's explicit cap, with no warning. The eval harness forces diff with max 600 on both gates for every mounted arm, so any gate whose shipped budget_cents exceeds 600 will refuse estimates in the eval that the shipped gate would accept.
findings.failure_mode: Opting into diff scaling silently lowers an explicitly configured budget; in the ablation, review-catch runs for gates with budget_cents > 600 exit 4 with status budget_exceeded and the arm is recorded as dissent-absent (reason budget), skewing the comparison against the shipped configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Either compute eff = max(conf, min(scaled, budget_cents_max)) so the ceiling only bounds the scaled growth, or log a WARN when budget_cents_max < conf and document that the ceiling wins.

findings.description: Two end-of-definition heuristics misfire on ordinary bash. (1) CLOSE_ONE (`\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$`) is searched over the whole header line, so a multi-line function whose header comment contains braces (e.g. `foo() {  # expands ${X}` or `# returns {k: v}`) is classified as a one-liner and its entire body loses its scope. (2) headers() measures indentation with expandtabs(8) but the closing-brace test uses `len(t) - len(t.lstrip())` on the raw line, so tab-indented functions never find their `}` and run to the next header instead.
findings.failure_mode: Same-scope (clause ii) credit is silently withheld for functions with brace-bearing header comments, and over-extended for tab-indented files, so recall under the new pm3_or_same_function rule under- or over-counts in ways that are not reproducible from the documented rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the one-liner test to the header's opening brace: strip a trailing `#…` comment first, then require the `{` that follows `()` and a `}` after it on the same line. Compute the closing-brace indentation with the same expandtabs(8) used in headers().

findings.description: When EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and the corpus fixture has no head/, the grader falls back to <workspace>/pr/head. The workspace is the agent-writable sandbox (review.md is written there by the agent). The new clause (ii) derives definition spans from those files, so a tampered head file (e.g. one ≤400-line function wrapping every defect site) would make a single citation anywhere in the file credit every defect. ablation-grade.sh's header in this diff states the harness never reads sandbox pr/.
findings.failure_mode: If ablation-grade.sh does not always export EVAL_HEAD_DIR, a review-catch trial whose fixture lacks head/ grades scope against agent-controlled files, letting an agent inflate recall; the result is indistinguishable from an honest grade.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the <workspace>/pr/head fallback (or gate it behind an explicit opt-in used only by self-check), and have ablation-grade.sh always pass EVAL_HEAD_DIR pointing at the pinned corpus fixture.

findings.description: The metadata object keeps additionalProperties: false and gains budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max, but the budget_exceeded envelope written in the same change also adds a new `reason: "budget"` key (and still carries estimated_cents, budget_cents, estimate_voices with a status value not in the enum). ablation-row.sh now reads `metadata.status == budget_exceeded` as a first-class state.
findings.failure_mode: Anyone validating the budget_exceeded envelope against the documentation contract gets a rejection on `reason`, and the contract no longer describes the envelope the row writer depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `reason`, `estimated_cents`, `budget_cents`, `estimate_voices` to the metadata properties and `budget_exceeded` to the status enum, or relax additionalProperties for the refusal envelope.

findings.description: The help text range was changed from a fixed line span to `sed -n '2,/^# ====/p'`. The script's visible section separators use `# --- … ---`, not `# ====`; if no line matches, sed prints from line 2 to end of file.
findings.failure_mode: `ablation-row.sh --help` dumps the entire script instead of the header.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm a `# ====` sentinel line exists immediately after the header comment, or anchor on an existing marker such as the first non-comment line.
